hypothesis: ORACLE CONTROL for 810: restart at the 49 KNOWN switch points, no detector. Separates 'restarting destroys shared knowledge' from 'the GLR detector over-fires'.
findings: DECISIVE CONTROL. With perfect detection (49/49, zero false alarms) cold restart reaches 59.60% - still 12.02pp BELOW the no-detector baseline's 71.62%. The GLR arm's extra shortfall to 47.51% is a further 12.09pp. So the cold-restart deficit splits almost exactly in half: half is the detector over-firing (recoverable by tuning), half is the cost of restarting AT ALL (not recoverable by any detector). Restart-on-change is the wrong architecture for this problem because the 10 loops share a transition structure - every loop is a path through IOBT_MAP - so knowledge of one loop transfers to the others, and a restart discards exactly that.
